rule: Server clock is a one-second timer that fires labels on minute, hour, weekday and day change. A siege session is a row (weekday, start hour inclusive, end hour exclusive, castle bitmask). Start order: announce, hold 1000 ms, set the server flag, then open the active zones and end the inactive ones. Respawn time = base + rnd() % variance, scaled by class percent (default 100), floored at 1000 ms. MVP = largest damage plus tanked among online, alive, same-map players; ties keep the earlier entry. Tomb appears after a fixed delay and names the killer and death time. Countdown = list of timed lines.
keep: one-second hold between announce and open, in a fixed order
server-owned siege flag; schedule checked once a minute on the server
tomb that names the killer and the time of death, after a fixed pause
respawn as base plus variance, scaled and floored
countdown as a list of timed lines
MVP as a damage ledger with a stable tie rule
change: castle bitmask becomes a zone id list (700 zones)
sessions are zone data, not script globals
schedule runs on the server tick, not a minute NPC label
no per-castle NPC labels; the zone state is the server state
MVP pick lives in the engine (parity row 18), not the NPC layer
tomb delay, pulse rate and countdown are client presentation only
look_test: Build a 20-second phone clip in three versions: (A) boss death, tomb after nine seconds naming the killer; (B) tomb at once; (C) siege start with a one-second hold before the zones light, against no hold. Dom compares which beat reads at 375 wide.
